_comment: Argon2id cross implementation vectors.
RFC 9106 Section 5 publishes Argon2id vectors, but every one of them
carries both a secret key and associated data. The pinned argon2 0.6.0
crate exposes a secret through new_with_secret and no associated data
input at all, so no RFC vector can be reproduced through the API mili
calls. These vectors cover the configuration mili actually uses:
Argon2id, version 19, a 32 byte tag, no secret and no associated data.
Each tag was produced by argon2-cffi 25.1.0, which binds the reference C
implementation, and each is checked against the independent pure Rust
implementation in the argon2 crate by
keyfile::tests::argon2id_vectors_from_the_reference_implementation. A
mismatch means the two implementations disagree, not that mili computed
something wrong, and that is the point of pinning both.
in_accepted_range records whether mili would accept that parameter set
on open. The out of range shapes are still derived through derive_kek so
that the pure Rust implementation is compared against the reference
implementation at those shapes too, but a key file naming them is
refused before any memory is reserved.
The inputs reuse RFC 9106 Section 5.3's own password and salt, as
interesting byte patterns, and not as an RFC claim.
